name: Ocient
tagline: Hyperscale data warehouse on NVMe compute-adjacent storage, rebranded as the OcientAIQ platform.
description: Ocient is a commercial MPP data warehouse built for continuously growing, trillion-row datasets in telecom, ad tech and government. Its compute-adjacent storage architecture puts large NVMe arrays inside each query node and bypasses the kernel for I/O, which keeps full scans fast and costs predictable at petabyte scale. Streaming loaders ingest from Kafka, and in-database ML and geospatial functions avoid data movement. The company now markets it as the OcientAIQ Unified Data Platform for AI workloads. It runs on-prem, in OcientCloud or in public clouds; it is a specialist system with a small user base.

pricing.notes: Enterprise subscriptions for on-prem, OcientCloud or public-cloud deployment.

scale.notes: Designed for multi-petabyte, trillion-row tables on NVMe-dense nodes.

strengths: Predictable performance on full scans of trillion-row tables
Compute-adjacent NVMe storage avoids network bottlenecks
weaknesses: Requires specialised NVMe-heavy hardware for on-prem
Limited public documentation and ecosystem integrations
useCases: Government and defense data at PB scale
notIdealFor: Self-service teams wanting a free tier
